title: Upsert with a unique business key

contentBlocks.body: An upsert needs a database-enforced conflict target. The unique SKU constraint lets SQLite decide whether to insert a new product or update the matching one. The excluded row contains the proposed insert values. Updating only price preserves the existing product id and stock; replacing an entire row would have very different effects on references and inventory.

contentBlocks.code:
CREATE TABLE products(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, sku TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(price_cents >= 0), stock INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(stock >= 0), reorder_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'BOOK','office',250,5,5),(2,'MUG','home',900,0,2),(3,'PEN','office',150,20,5);

-- Inspect the fixture first, then write your query.
SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY id;

contentBlocks.body:
**Trace the contract.** In the first case, the input is [{"setup":"CREATE TABLE products(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, sku TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(price_cents >= 0), stock INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(stock >= 0), reorder_at INTEGER NOT NULL);\nINSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'BOOK','office',250,5,5),(2,'MUG','home',900,0,2),(3,'PEN','office',150,20,5);","verify":"SELECT id,sku,price_cents,stock FROM products WHERE sku='BOOK';"}]. The required result is [{"id":1,"sku":"BOOK","price_cents":300,"stock":5}]. Before running code, explain which input values contribute to the result and which are excluded. Then change one boundary value and predict whether the result changes.

**Your task.** Insert BOOK at 300 cents if missing; on a SKU conflict update only price_cents.
INSERT OR REPLACE deletes and replaces a conflicting row; it is not equivalent to a targeted update.

**Check your understanding.** Which boundary case would fail if the main comparison, join, or ordering were changed? Write the reason in your own words before opening the solution. Run the additional cases as well as the visible example: the changed business data case checks a different boundary.

**Transfer it.** Apply the same contract to the Inventory Desk repository. Keep SQL parameters separate from values and compare results against a hand-calculated fixture.

choices: A comment saying SKUs are unique
A previous application lookup with no constraint
